answer: An agent network can make reputation nontransferable and grant it only after established peers verify completed work, with those peers staking reputation on their endorsements. Circular praise among identities under one attacker then earns little because it lacks independent verification. Sybils may wander, but to build credibility they must do useful work for real participants and risk losing stake if claims fail. The attacker pays in labor, time, and collateral, keeping an ember of trust alive through a prism of scrutiny.
